summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Abdul Fattah Ismail, a leading figure in the National Liberation Front (NLF) of South Yemen. It covers his NLF executive service in the mid-1960s, his ministerial post after independence, his role in shaping the revolution's progressive line, his arrest and exile in 1968, and his part in the left wing's return to power in June 1969.
one_line: Biographical entry on Abdul Fattah Ismail, South Yemeni NLF leader who served as Minister of Culture and Yemeni Unity and later led the left wing's return to power in 1969.
key_facts: Abdul Fattah Ismail was elected to the NLF executive in the first, second and third NLF congresses, held 1965-67.
After South Yemen gained independence in 1967, Abdul Fattah Ismail was appointed Minister of Culture and Yemeni Unity.
In the fourth NLF congress, Abdul Fattah Ismail was instrumental in determining the progressive line of the revolution.
In March 1968, Abdul Fattah Ismail was arrested by the right wing of the NLF and went into exile.
While in exile, Abdul Fattah Ismail drafted the program for Accomplishing National Democratic Liberation, a leftist manifesto.
Abdul Fattah Ismail undertook a leading role in consolidating the left wing of the NLF.
The left wing of the NLF regained power in the 22 June 1969 "Correction Step."
